chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever loves a disbeliever has indeed hated God, and whoever hates a disbeliever has indeed loved God.
Then he (peace be upon him) said: The friend of the enemy of God is the enemy of God.

key_terms.أبغض: To hate, to harbor enmity toward
key_terms.كافر: Kafir - a disbeliever, one who rejects faith in God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about befriending the enemies of God?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that love and hatred must be aligned with faith: loving those who disbelieve in God is tantamount to hating God, while dissociating from disbelief is an expression of love for God. He further emphasizes that befriending the enemies of God makes one an enemy of God. This teaching, delivered in a scholarly assembly recorded by al-Saduq in Rajab 368 AH, reflects the Quranic doctrine of al-walaya wa al-bara'a (loyalty and disavowal), a foundational principle in Shia theology regarding the proper orientation of one's allegiances.
